title: How does coax learn that a background shell command ended?
body:
coax's report to decade carries a `subagents` list (461c197). `Snapshot::of` in `report.rs` fills it from `Transcript::subagents`, which returns the top-level tool calls that start a sub-agent, the `Agent` or `Task` calls. A shell command the agent runs in the background is an ordinary tool call, and coax does not track it after the call completes. decade's `Subagent` is described as "a sub-agent or background task", so such a command belongs in the list too.

## Open

- What the Claude adapter v0.101.0 sends for a background shell command: whether its tool call stays in progress, completes at launch, or gets a later update when the command ends. The answer is in the adapter's bundled JavaScript or in a log of a live session.
- If nothing marks the end, whether coax can tell a background command is done at all.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/72a5a67e
notes.text:
Checked against the adapter's source, in a checkout of `claude-agent-acp` a little ahead of v0.101.0.

- A background Bash call goes `completed` at launch, with a result like "Command running in background with ID …". The adapter sends coax nothing more on that call.
- The adapter receives the SDK's `task_started`, `task_notification` and `background_tasks_changed` frames. It passes them on only to a client that declares the JetBrains AIR `asyncTasks` capability or the `terminal_output` meta. coax declares neither, in `src/acp.rs`.
- The adapter never holds a turn for a background shell. The comment on `liveBackgroundTasks` in `acp-agent.ts` says a hold must never wait on a shell.
- `_session/async_task/stop` takes `{sessionId, asyncTaskId}` and returns `{stopped}`. It works only for AIR clients. No method lists tasks.
- Not traced to the end: when the command exits, Claude Code probably wakes the model with a follow-up turn (`startAutonomousCycle`). coax would see that turn as agent text with no prompt open.

So coax cannot show a background command without declaring a new capability.

| path | what coax gets | cost |
|---|---|---|
| declare `terminal_output` | a terminal kept open on the call until the command ends, with its output and exit | coax handles terminal updates on every Bash call, foreground ones too |
| declare AIR `asyncTasks` | a full task lifecycle, and stopping | AIR changes other behaviour too, such as background sub-agents no longer holding the turn |
| read the launch result's text | the task's ID, and perhaps its end from the follow-up turn | no reliable end signal |

The lean is `terminal_output`, the one path with a real end signal that does not bring the rest of AIR. What declaring it changes for ordinary Bash calls is being read next.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/72a5a67e
notes.text:
What declaring `terminal_output` changes, read in the same adapter checkout.

- A client declares it with `"terminal_output": true` in `clientCapabilities._meta` (`ClientCapabilities.from` in `tool-calls/client-capabilities.ts`). The adapter does not read `terminal: true`. In coax this is one more key in the `_meta` map in `src/acp.rs`.
- Foreground Bash: the `tool_call` carries `_meta.terminal_info {terminal_id}`, and its `content` becomes `{"type": "terminal", "terminalId": ...}`. At the result the adapter sends one update with `_meta.terminal_output {terminal_id, data}` holding the whole output. A second update carries the status and `_meta.terminal_exit {terminal_id, exit_code, signal}`. The output no longer arrives as a text block in `content`, and `rawOutput` is left out. Nothing streams before the result.
- Background Bash: the call goes `completed` at launch, with the launch text in `terminal_output`. `withRunningTerminal` holds back `terminal_exit`. When the task ends, `endBackgroundTask` calls `taskEnded` in `background-work.ts`, which sends `terminal_exit` with `exit_code` null, killed or not. The status does not change. No output arrives while the command runs, since the live tail runs only for ACP v2 clients.
- If the session ends before the command, the adapter sends no `terminal_exit` to a v1 client.
- Reading the source found no effect on turn holds, sub-agents, queued prompts or permission requests.

Not confirmed: that the SDK's `task_notification` reaches `endBackgroundTask` for a client like coax, and that replay on `session/load` sends the terminal messages too. A live trial with a logged session would settle both.

Cost for coax: `Transcript` keeps no `_meta` beyond the parent link, and stores only `content`. Once coax declares the meta, Bash output moves out of `content`, so coax has to keep `terminal_output` and `terminal_exit` itself. Without that, Bash output would disappear from the transcript.
